rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are capped at the lower of 3% or 80% of the 12-month CPI change; no increase if CPI is negative. The current allowable increase for Sept 1, 2026 to Aug 31, 2027 is 2.87%. Owners must give written notice of the ordinance at lease start or with any rent increase notice.
citation_aliases: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period
rules.effective_date_note: Per city announcement (D085), the ordinances were not effective until November 19, 2021; the allowable increase is published by June 30 each year, effective September 1.
rules.exemptions: Buildings constructed after Feb 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent after Jan 1, 1990. Owners may petition for relief for a fair and reasonable return.
rules.interaction: Local cap applies instead of the state cap where both cover a unit.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner petition for fair return relief
mobile home spaces offered for rent after Jan 1, 1990

rules.review_note: Documents give no ordinance number or code section; citation is descriptive.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner may not end a tenancy without a just cause stated in a written notice, and must first give notice of a curable violation. For no-fault terminations the owner must give 3 months of relocation assistance or waive the last 3 months of rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 30 days; 3 months relocation for no-fault
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (adopted 2021)
citation_aliases: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice
rules.effective_date_note: Per city announcement (D085); owners had to notify existing tenants before December 19, 2021.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters.
rules.interaction: Local ordinance governs instead of the state just-cause law where both apply.
rules.review_note: Documents give no ordinance number or code section; citation is descriptive.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell, license or provide, algorithmic rent-setting software that uses nonpublic competitor data for Santa Ana residential rentals. Tenants can sue for injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation per month, plus attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation per month
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.effective_date_note: Stated as effective April 2, 2026 in the Morgan Lewis alert (D002/D037); news items show first reading Feb. 17, 2026 and final vote set for March 3, 2026.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation per month, damages, injunctive relief, attorney's fees; also code enforcement
rules.exemptions: Pricing software relying solely on public data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements

unverifiable_exemptions: tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements

rules.review_note: Ordinance number and effective date come only from the law-firm alert; the news articles do not state them.

parsed.notes: Santa Ana has three records: rent stabilization (c74 and c76), just cause (c75 and c77) and the algorithmic rent-setting ban (c81, c94, c102 and c103). None of the documents covers city-level security deposits, application or screening fees, or screening restrictions. I made no no-rule findings for those categories. State rules (Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1950.5 and 1950.6, Gov. Code § 12955) may apply there.
